transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-16 15:00 PST
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sofia Kim (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CSM); Maya Gupta, Alex Torres, Jin Park, Priya Nair (Orion)

Summary: quick weekly sync for POC quality evals, discussed a small regression in customer prompt set v1, explored guardrail tuning and scoring thresholds, agreed on next steps to push prompt_set_v2 and run regression suite.

Topics: quality metrics, prompt sets, scoring calibration, guardrails, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security questions (KMS, audit logs).

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda is one, review the latest quality numbers two, dig into the regression you found maya three, propose next steps and owners.
00:18 Maya: thanks, yeah we've been running the evaluation over last week on your hosted endpoint, we saw a drop in factuality on the clinical summarization set around dec 10th, it's ~6 point drop depending on the metric.
00:33 Ethan: ok can you remind me which prompt set and model variant, was this prompt_set_v1 with the quantized-4bit runtime?
00:42 Maya: correct, prompt_set_v1, model variant rdx-3b-quant4, and we also tested rdx-3b-fp16 as a control. The fp16 seemed a hair better but cost was higher.
00:55 Alex: and the scoring we used was a blended rubric, rouge+factuality score from our annotators, threshold set at 0.87 for pass.
01:08 Sofia: good, quick clarification: when you say factuality drop, is that relative to baseline results from our first week or relative to last week's run?
01:17 Maya: relative to baseline from two weeks ago, before we switched in the KV cache optimization you rolled out. We thought K V cache might cause some prefix mismatch?
01:29 Ethan: hmm that makes sense — we shipped a minor change to continuous batching / cache eviction logic last week; it shouldn't impact generation semantics but could affect prefix alignment for long-context prompts.
01:40 Jin: from security side we logged nothing anomalous, just wanted to flag that for our audit path. Also we need the exact change log for the runtime update for our compliance team.
01:51 Sofia: will do, i'll attach the changelog link after the call. link: https://redwood-cloud.internal/changelogs/rdx-3b-cache-2025-12-09
02:03 Priya: one more thing — a handful of outputs triggered our guardrail classifier and were getting truncated. We saw more false positives after the change, which affects measured quality because annotators mark them as failures.
02:17 Ethan: ok that points to two separate vectors: generation drift vs guardrail sensitivity. We can address guardrail thresholds quickly; generation drift we need to reproduce.
02:28 Maya: i uploaded the sample failing prompts into the shared sheet — see: https://shared.company/docs/orion/redwood/prompt_fails.csv — feel free to reference, some examples are long EHR summaries ~1.8k tokens.
02:44 Sofia: thanks, we'll pull those. Ethan, can you walk through our proposed repro steps?
02:49 Ethan: sure. step one: run the same prompt set through our fp16 and quant4 backends to compare token-by-token logits and final output differences. step two: rerun with cache disabled to see if prefix alignment changes. step three: adjust guardrail classifier threshold and re-score. step four: run annotator subset to validate.
03:12 Alex: about costs, if we move to fp16 to chase quality, can you quantify delta? we need approximate per 1k tokens.
03:22 Ethan: rough numbers: hosted quant4 is ~0.6x cost of fp16 on per-token base, fp16 higher but latency also different. we can give a spreadsheet with per-route breakdown.
03:32 Sofia: we'll push updated cost table with the scoring sheet.
03:36 Maya: on scoring, we noticed some instability in how our automated factuality metric correlates with human labels; the precision dropped more than recall, so false positives in flagged hallucinations.
03:49 Ethan: that's probably coupled with the guardrail threshold — if classifier gets more conservative after the runtime tweak, you'll see more false positives. We'll test lowering sensitivity by 0.1 and re-evaluate.
04:02 Priya: also from product POV we need consistent behavior for edge-case long prompts — can't have outputs truncated unpredictably.
04:11 Sofia: agreed. quick question to team: are we ok to run a controlled performance test with caching off in staging? that will cost some cycles but necessary to isolate.
04:20 Maya: yes we can run it overnight, we'll allocate staging capacity.
04:25 Ethan: perfect. i'll schedule a run and capture logs, hoping to reproduce the delta by noon tomorrow.
04:33 Jin: what about the audit logs for those runs, we need detailed request/response hashes not raw PII. can you stream only hashes to our S3?
04:44 Sofia: yes we support hashed logs and we can turn on that option for your account, i'll confirm retention policy.
04:51 Jin: also we need to validate the KMS flow for model keys; redwood integration doc we saw was generic, please send the specific flow for VPC/private deployment.
05:04 Sofia: will include the KMS/HSM diagram in the docs packet (see next steps).
05:11 Ethan: returning to technical repro: for the long EHR prompts, we noticed the KV cache eviction boundary might be misaligned if tokens are counted differently between tokenizer versions; could be tokenizer mismatch between your preprocessing and our runtime.
05:26 Alex: interesting, we did a tokenizer move in our pipeline two weeks ago; good catch. we'll verify tokenization versions.
05:33 Maya: okay that could explain much — if token counts differ our prefix windows shift and cache hits become misses resulting in changed outputs.
05:44 Ethan: yes, so step A for you: pin tokenizer to v2025-11-01 or run our tokenizer as part of pipeline. step B for us: run the no-cache test to see if outputs match expected baseline.
05:58 Sofia: i'd like to discuss guardrails briefly — currently you have a conservative toxicity/factuality classifier. we can relax thresholds or add exception lists for clinical terms to reduce false positives.
06:12 Priya: exception lists sound risky from safety side but useful for specialist vocab. maybe a whitelist approach where certain phrases bypass classifier if matched with high-confidence factual cues.
06:27 Ethan: we can implement fuzzy whitelist matching and require two-tier checks: classifier + semantic similarity to allowed patterns. that'll cut false positives.
06:38 Maya: sounds good. how long to implement that on our POC tenant?
06:42 Ethan: quick patch to thresholds is hours, whitelist integration a couple days for safe testing.
06:49 Sofia: note that whitelist needs to be auditable for compliance. include change log entries.
06:55 Jin: yes auditability is key. please include who approved any whitelist changes.
07:01 Sofia: noted. we'll attach approval metadata.
07:06 Alex: can we talk about scoring rubric changes? we want to reduce false failure rate by weighting human-annotator trust higher for edge cases.
07:17 Ethan: recommended config: weight human labels 0.7, auto-metric 0.3, and treat guardrail failures separately so they don't automatically count as full failure unless confirmed by annotator.
07:31 Maya: that makes sense. our annotators can re-review flagged cases. we want to keep regression detection sensitive but avoid noisy alerts.
07:43 Sofia: ok we'll prepare scoring_v2 and push to shared sheet, along with a mapping of how fail/pass decisions map to CI alerts.
07:54 Ethan: two more notes — we saw one outlier batch where latency spiked by ~120ms for a subset of requests. not sure it's related but we captured traces.
08:06 Maya: yes we saw that correlated with batch size auto-scaling hitting a small window. we think autoscaler ramp up caused slightly older kernels to handle load briefly.
08:19 Ethan: we can pin batch size for sensitive routes to avoid variance; also schedule a kernel pre-warm for the timeline of your regression runs.
08:31 Sofia: i'll share recommended autoscale config for your POC routes.
08:36 Maya: great. also, i'm worried about the spike in guardrail false positives after your change — do you have historical FPR numbers?
08:44 Ethan: baseline FPR was ~2.3% on your clinical set, recent run showed ~6.7%. we're targeting back to <=3%.
08:53 Priya: that's a big jump. ok let's prioritize threshold rollback and whitelist for a quick fix.
09:00 Ethan: yes quick fix tonight, whitelist work in next 48hrs.
09:07 Sofia: next topic: rollout policy. if the fp16 run is better but cost is 1.5x, do you want to keep a mixed strategy? dedicate critical routes to fp16 and background to quant4?
09:18 Alex: yes that fits our cost goals. critical summarization routes can be fp16, less critical can be quant4. need explicit per-route latency SLOs.
09:27 Sofia: we can set per-route model pins and automatic fallback to alter variant if capacity constrained. that'll keep availability.
09:35 Jin: and can we enforce region pinning for data residency? some of our patients are EU-based.
09:43 Sofia: yes we have regional routing and private deployment options, we'll add a note to the architecture doc.
09:50 Ethan: quick KPI check: what's your acceptance criteria to move POC to pilot?
09:56 Maya: primary metric is pass rate >= 0.9 on our annotated clinical set and guardrail FPR <= 3% for two consecutive runs. also latency p95 < 650ms for critical routes.
10:11 Sofia: good clear goals. we'll tailor the scoring_v2 to that and run two validation runs.
10:18 Alex: about documentation, can you share the exact prompt_set_v2 changes? we want to see prompt templates and instruction tuning changes.
10:25 Sofia: we'll push a diff: prompt_set_v2 includes fewer system-level instructions, explicit role tags, and added clarifying examples for clinical terms.
10:36 Ethan: also we'll include tokenization normalization steps to avoid mismatches.
10:42 Maya: perfect. one peripheral ask: can you put a quick eval harness in our repo so we can run nightly checks?
10:50 Sofia: yes we have a lightweight CLI eval harness we can share as a repo; i'll open access.
11:00 Priya: on security again, Jin needs SOC2 artifacts and the network diagram for our legal review.
11:06 Sofia: sending SOC2 report and network diagram (see next steps), i'll also include retention and KMS config.
11:14 Jin: please ensure data is encrypted at rest and in transit and that de-id practices are documented for PII.
11:21 Sofia: we already use TLS and provide encryption at rest via KMS, and we can provide de-identification guidance.
11:28 Ethan: ok quick recap of technical owners and timeline: ethan will run no-cache tests and latency traces (due 2025-12-20), sofia to share prompt_set_v2 & scoring (due 2025-12-18), maya to run regressions and upload results (due 2025-12-22), jin to confirm KMS/controls (due 2025-12-19).
11:52 Maya: noted. any other blockers?
12:00 Alex: none from infra; we'll verify tokenizer pinned version today.
12:06 Priya: product team ok with the whitelist approach as long as audit trail exists.
12:12 Sofia: great. last thing — i'll send a calendar invite for a follow-up deep-dive if regressions persist, otherwise next weekly sync same time next week.
12:22 Ethan: thanks everyone. i'll post the initial no-cache test results in the shared thread.
12:28 Sofia: closing notes: attached links — prompt diff: https://shared.company/docs/orion/redwood/prompt_set_v2_diff.pdf, scoring sheet: https://sheets.company/scoring/redwood-orion-v2, changelog: https://redwood-cloud.internal/changelogs/rdx-3b-cache-2025-12-09
12:40 Maya: thanks all, talk soon.
12:45 [call ends]
